Original page actually read, key points24–26 and urgent warning subsections; postpartum heavy bleeding129–133 includes≥1pad/hour, clots larger than egg/tissue;152 disclosure of pregnancy during prior year;153 attributes warning signs to AIM. CDC-hosted AIM material is one group, not two. General pregnancy/year-after-birth safety resource; the one-year warning window is not the definition of secondary PPH.

Official WHO IRIS PDF downloaded and actual text read: PDF50–52/printed32–34 (recommendations14–15 TXA prophylaxis), PDF57–58/printed39–40 (recommendation22 therapeutic early trigger, vaginal-predominant evidence and limited caesarean data), PDF60–65/printed42–47 (recommendations24–30 drugs/massage/TXA/fluids/bundle/retained placenta), PDF74–78/printed56–60 (transfusion/supportive care/iron). Only these passages attested; no image algorithm reproduced. Joint WHO/FIGO/ICM writing is one group; news pages, Bookshelf copies and society reposts are not additional independent evidence. EBCOG commentary discusses this guideline; Cochrane reviews partly WHO funded and contribute common upstream trials.

Official EBCOG-hosted two-page commentary PDF downloaded and prose/authors/references actually read. Page1 Comment first paragraph explicitly discusses measured loss≥300mL with abnormal vital signs for earlier action; page1 also comments on team readiness, training and debrief. DOI10.1016/j.ejogrb.2025.114798, online2025-10-27, journal316 January2026. Independent commentary writing by Zaigham/Louwen/Mukhopadhyay/Mahmood, not a separate trial or second evidence base. Louwen also FIGO president; shared institutional role and WHO upstream disclosed. It does not independently state every branch of WHO recommendation22.

Original Cochrane plain-language summary and full abstract actually read(web43–120), DOI10.1002/14651858.CD007872.pub4: three trials18,974, little/no prophylactic blood-loss benefit, rare serious harms uncertain. Search to2024-09-06; WHO partially funded review. Same review-team group as caesarean review; common trials with WHO guidance, not independent trial replication.

Original plain-language summary/abstract actually read: six trials15,981 mostly low-risk participants; little/no measured or estimated≥1000mL reduction, slight calculated-loss benefit; serious rare harms uncertain. Evidence through2024-02-20. WHO partly funded; same review team as vaginal review, shared studies informing WHO2025. Not presented as evidence that every possible high-risk subgroup lacks benefit.

Actual official HTML fetched and read recommendation1.4.2: do not offer prostaglandinF2alpha(carboprost) to women with asthma because of bronchospasm.2019 recommendation, exact latest page date not extracted. Bounded asthma/drug selection passage only, not full evidence review or all guidance. Same NICE editorial group as NG235; UK asthma recommendation is stronger than product-label caution.

Original SmPC actual sections4.4(web265–269) history of asthma and bronchoconstriction caution;4.8(331–334) respiratory adverse effects;5.1(364) uterine action; section10 revision05/2022 (no exact day). Manufacturer-authored regulatory label, distinct writing from NICE. Caution in label is not falsely equated to NICE avoid-in-asthma recommendation. No dose/route recipe reproduced.

Original article’s indexed Thromboprophylaxis section and recommendation50 actually read, DOI10.2450/2019.0245-18: PPH/transfusion increase postpartum VTE risk; severe/massive PPH requires individualized prophylaxis after bleeding controlled and coagulopathy corrected. Author/methods abstract also read; full direct PMC page returned recaptcha, not attested as full article. Cites observational studies151–152 and other guidelines; joint institutional overlap with later WHO/EBCOG acknowledged. Independent NATA writing corroborates RCOG; not separate trial replication.
